chunks.st: is likened to both a donkey driver, who walks behind the animal and prods it, and a camel driver, who walks before the animal and leads it, in the sense that he is pulled in two opposite directions. Due to the uncertainty with regard to the location of his Shabbat limit, his movement is restricted as though his residence was established in both his city and at a location along the way to the other city. He may not venture beyond two thousand cubits from either location.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who went out past his Shabbos limit, or was outside it when Shabbos started, may not come back in. Some Rabbis say a little bit outside is still all right.

chunks.en: Someone who went out past the Shabbos limit,
chunks.st: One who intentionally, not for the purpose of performing a mitzva, went out beyond his Shabbat limit,

chunks.en: even one amah,
chunks.st: even if only one cubit,

chunks.en: may not come back in.
chunks.st: may not reenter.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: two amos, he may come in,
chunks.st: If he went out two cubits he may reenter;

chunks.en: three, he may not come in.
chunks.st: however, if he went out three cubits he may not reenter.

chunks.en: Someone who was outside the Shabbos limit when it got dark,
chunks.st: With regard to one for whom it grew dark while he was traveling outside the Shabbat limit of the town where he was heading,

chunks.en: even one amah,
chunks.st: even if he was only one cubit

chunks.en: may not go in.
chunks.st: outside the limit he may not enter the town.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even fifteen amos,
chunks.st: Even if he was fifteen cubits

chunks.he: יִכָּנֵס, שֶׁאֵין הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת מְמַצִּין אֶת הַמִּדּוֹת,
chunks.en: he may go in, because the measurers do not mark the full amount,
chunks.st: beyond the limit he may enter the town, because the surveyors do not precisely demarcate the measures;
chunks.stMore: rather, they mark the Shabbat limit within the two thousand cubits,

chunks.en: because of people who make mistakes.
chunks.st: due to those who err.

mishnayos.summary: Before we measure the 2000 amos around a city, we straighten its edges: houses or buildings that stick out count as if the whole side reached them, and we make the city into a square.

chunks.en: How do we stretch out the edges of cities?
chunks.st: How does one extend the boundaries of cities
chunks.stMore: in order to ensure that all its protrusions are included within the borders of the city?

chunks.en: If one house is pushed in and another sticks out,
chunks.st: He extends a straight line across the edge of the city, and if a house is recessed and another house protrudes,

chunks.en: or a tower is pushed in and another sticks out,
chunks.st: or a turret [pagum] is recessed and another turret protrudes

chunks.he: הָיוּ שָׁם גְּדוּדִיּוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: or there were broken walls ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: from that line, and similarly, if there were remnants of walls ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: and bridges and grave monuments,
chunks.st: and bridges and monuments

words.note: Small buildings over graves.

chunks.en: that have a place to live in them,
chunks.st: over graves in which there is a residence,

chunks.en: we stretch the measure out as far as them,
chunks.st: one extends the measure of that side of the city as though there were other structures opposite them
chunks.stMore: in the adjacent corner of the city.

chunks.en: and we make the city like a square board,
chunks.st: And prior to measuring the Shabbat limit, one renders the city like a square tablet

chunks.en: so that it gains the corners.
chunks.st: so that it gains the corners, although there are actually no houses in those corners.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir says we add a karpef, about seventy amos, to every city before measuring. The Sages say it is only used to join two cities that are close together.

chunks.en: We give a karpef to a city,
chunks.st: One allocates a karpef to every city,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the measure of a karpef, which is slightly more than seventy cubits, is added to every city, and the two thousand cubits of the Shabbat limit are measured from there;

words.note: A space of about seventy amos.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they only spoke of a karpef
chunks.st: They spoke of the addition of a karpef only

chunks.en: between two towns.
chunks.st: with regard to the space between two adjacent cities.

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ לָזוֹ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם,
chunks.en: If this one has seventy amos and a bit,
chunks.st: How so? If this city has seventy cubits and a remainder

chunks.en: and that one has seventy amos and a bit,
chunks.st: vacant on one side, and that city has seventy cubits and a remainder
chunks.stMore: vacant on the adjacent side, and the two areas of seventy-plus cubits overlap,

chunks.en: he makes one karpef for both of them, to make them like one town.
chunks.st: the karpef combines the two cities into one.

mishnayos.summary: Three villages standing in a triangle can count as one town if the middle village fills the gap between the two outer ones.

chunks.en: And also three villages in a triangle,
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of three villages that are arranged as a triangle,

chunks.en: if between the two outer ones there is
chunks.st: if there are only

chunks.en: one hundred forty-one and a third amos,
chunks.st: 141⅓ cubits separating between the two outer villages,

chunks.he: עָשָׂה אֶמְצָעִי אֶת שְׁלָשְׁתָּן לִהְיוֹתָן כְּאֶחָד:
chunks.en: the middle one makes all three of them like one.
chunks.st: the middle village combines the three villages into one.

mishnayos.summary: We measure the Shabbos limit with a fifty amah rope held at the heart. Valleys, fences and hills are skipped over as if the ground were flat.

chunks.en: We only measure with a rope
chunks.st: One may measure a Shabbat limit only with a rope fifty cubits

chunks.en: of fifty amos,
chunks.st: long,

chunks.en: not less and not more.
chunks.st: no less and no more,
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And he must measure only at the height of his heart.
chunks.st: And one may measure the limit only at the level of one’s heart,
chunks.stMore: i.e., whoever comes to measure the limit must hold the rope next to his chest.

chunks.he: הָיָה מוֹדֵד וְהִגִּיעַ לְגַיְא אוֹ לְגָדֵר,
chunks.en: If he was measuring and came to a valley or a fence,
chunks.st: If one was measuring the limit and he reached a canyon or a fence,
chunks.stMore: the height of the fence and the depth of the canyon are not counted toward the two thousand cubits; rather,

chunks.en: he skips over it and goes back to measuring.
chunks.st: he spans it and then resumes his measurement.
chunks.stMore: Two people hold the two ends of the rope straight across the canyon or the fence, and the distance is measured as though the area were completely flat.

chunks.en: If he came to a hill,
chunks.st: If one reached a hill,
chunks.stMore: he does not measure its height; rather,

chunks.en: he skips over it and goes back to measuring,
chunks.st: he spans the hill as if it were not there and then resumes his measurement,

chunks.en: as long as he does not go out past the Shabbos limit.
chunks.st: provided he does not thereby go out beyond the city’s Shabbat limit,
chunks.stMore: as those watching the surveyor might mistakenly think the limit extends to that point.

chunks.en: If he cannot skip over it,
chunks.st: If, due to the width of the canyon or hill, he cannot span it,

chunks.en: about this Rabbi Dostai son of
chunks.st: with regard to this situation Rabbi Dostai bar Yannai said

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yannai said in the name of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.st: in the name of Rabbi Meir:

chunks.en: I heard that we measure through hills.
chunks.explain: As if there were a tunnel straight through.
chunks.st: I heard that one may pierce hills. In other words, one measures the distance as if there were a hole from one side of the hill to the other, so that in effect, he measures only the horizontal distance and ignores the differences in elevation.

mishnayos.summary: Only an expert may measure the Shabbos limit. If the measurements are different, we follow the longer one, and even a servant is believed about where the limit is, because these rules are meant to be easy.

chunks.en: We only measure with an expert.
chunks.st: One may measure the Shabbat limit only with an expert surveyor.

chunks.he: רִבָּה לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד וּמִעֵט לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
chunks.en: If he made it longer in one place and shorter in another place,
chunks.st: If it is discovered that the surveyor extended the limit in one place and reduced it in another place,
chunks.stMore: so that the line marking the Shabbat limit is not straight,

chunks.en: we listen to the place where he made it longer.
chunks.st: one accepts the measurement of the place where he extended
chunks.stMore: the limit and straightens the limit accordingly.

chunks.en: If he made it longer for one and shorter for another,
chunks.st: Similarly, if the surveyor extended the limit for one and reduced it for another,

chunks.en: we listen to the longer one.
chunks.st: one accepts the extended measurement.

chunks.en: Even a servant,
chunks.st: And furthermore, even a gentile slave

chunks.en: even a maid,
chunks.st: and even a gentile maidservant,
chunks.stMore: whose testimonies are generally considered unreliable,

chunks.en: are believed to say,
chunks.st: are trustworthy to say:

chunks.en: Until here is the Shabbos limit,
chunks.st: The Shabbat limit extended until here;

chunks.en: because the Sages did not say this
chunks.st: as the Sages did not state the matter,
chunks.stMore: the laws of Shabbat limits,

chunks.en: to be strict, but to be easy.
chunks.st: to be stringent, but rather to be lenient. The prohibition to walk more than two thousand cubits is rabbinic in origin and is therefore interpreted leniently.

mishnayos.summary: May one eiruv be made for a whole city? If it grew from a private town into a public city, yes. If it was public and became private, a part must be left out so people do not forget the rules of eiruv.

chunks.he: עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים,
chunks.en: A private town that became a public city,
chunks.st: If a private city, which does not have many residents, grows and becomes a heavily populated public city,

chunks.en: we may make an eiruv for all of it.
chunks.st: one may establish a joining of the courtyards for all of it,
chunks.stMore: as long as it does not include a public domain as defined by Torah law.

chunks.en: But one that was public and became private,
chunks.st: And if a public city loses residents over time and becomes a private city,

chunks.en: we may not make an eiruv for all of it,
chunks.st: one may not establish an eiruv for all of it

chunks.en: unless he leaves out a part outside it
chunks.st: unless one maintains an area outside the eiruv

chunks.en: like the town of Chadashah in Yehudah,
chunks.st: that is like the size of the city of Ḥadasha in Judea,

chunks.en: which has fifty people living in it,
chunks.st: which has fifty residents.
chunks.stMore: Carrying within the eiruv is permitted, but it remains prohibited to carry in the area excluded from the eiruv. The reason for this requirement is to ensure that the laws of eiruv will not be forgotten.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: The excluded area need not be so large;

chunks.en: three courtyards with two houses each.
chunks.st: rather, it is sufficient to exclude three courtyards with two houses each.

mishnayos.stIntro: Although this chapter as a whole deals with halakhot governing the joining of Shabbat boundaries, this mishna returns to the halakhot governing a joining of courtyards.

mishnayos.summary: A person can only make his Shabbos home somewhere within 2000 amos of where he is when Shabbos starts. An eiruv put just outside the city does not help, and one put farther out gives on one side but takes away on the other.

chunks.en: Someone who was east of home and told his son,
chunks.st: One who was to the east of his home when Shabbat began, and he had said to his son
chunks.stMore: before Shabbat:

chunks.en: Make an eiruv for me in the west,
chunks.st: Establish an eiruv for me to the west;

chunks.en: or west of home and told his son,
chunks.st: or, if he was to the west of his home and he had said to his son:

chunks.en: Make an eiruv for me in the east,
chunks.st: Establish an eiruv for me to the east,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ הֵימֶנּוּ וּלְבֵיתוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: if from him to his house is two thousand amos,
chunks.st: the halakha is as follows: If there is a distance of two thousand cubits from his current location to his house, and

chunks.en: and to his eiruv more than that,
chunks.st: the distance to his eiruv is greater than this,

chunks.en: he may go to his house but not to his eiruv.
chunks.st: he is permitted to walk to his house, and from there he may walk two thousand cubits in every direction, but it is prohibited for him to walk to the spot where his son had deposited his eiruv.

chunks.en: If to his eiruv is two thousand amos,
chunks.st: If the distance from one’s current location to his eiruv is two thousand cubits,

chunks.en: and to his house more than that,
chunks.st: and the distance to his house is greater than this,

chunks.en: he may not go to his house but may go to his eiruv.
chunks.st: he is prohibited from walking to his house, and he is permitted to walk to the spot of his eiruv,
chunks.stMore: and from there he may walk two thousand cubits in every direction. In other words, with regard to the Shabbat limit, one’s place of residence for Shabbat cannot be more than two thousand cubits from his physical location when Shabbat begins.

chunks.he: הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְעִבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר,
chunks.en: Someone who puts his eiruv in the edge area of the city
chunks.st: One who places his eiruv in the outskirts of the city,
chunks.stMore: i.e., within an area of slightly more than seventy cubits surrounding the city,

chunks.en: has done nothing at all.
chunks.st: it is as though he has not done anything.
chunks.stMore: The two thousand cubits of one’s Shabbat limit are measured from the edge of the outskirts of the city even if there is no eiruv, and one therefore gains nothing from placing an eiruv within this area.

chunks.en: If he put it outside the city's limit,
chunks.st: If, however, he placed his eiruv outside the city’s boundary,

chunks.en: even one amah,
chunks.st: even if he placed it only one cubit
chunks.stMore: beyond the city,

chunks.en: what he gains he loses.
chunks.st: what he gains in distance through his eiruv on one side of the city he loses on the other side.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who puts his eiruv in another city may walk through that whole city and then 2000 amos more. Rabbi Akiva says he only gets 2000 amos from the eiruv.

chunks.en: People of a big city may walk
chunks.st: The residents of a large city may walk

chunks.en: through all of a small city,
chunks.st: through an entire small city,

chunks.en: but people of a small city may not walk
chunks.st: and the residents of a small city may not walk

chunks.en: through all of a big city.
chunks.st: through an entire large city,
chunks.stMore: even if part of it is located more than two thousand cubits from their city.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. מִי שֶׁהָיָה בְעִיר גְּדוֹלָה וְנָתַן
chunks.en: How is this? Someone who was in a big city and put
chunks.st: How so? One who was in a large city and

chunks.en: his eiruv in a small city,
chunks.st: placed his eiruv in a small city,

chunks.en: or in a small city and put
chunks.st: or one who was in a small city and placed

chunks.en: his eiruv in a big city,
chunks.st: his eiruv in a large city,

chunks.en: walks through all of it and outside
chunks.st: may walk through the entire city in which he placed his eiruv and

chunks.en: of it two thousand amos.
chunks.st: another two thousand cubits beyond it,
chunks.stMore: as the entire city is considered as though it were only four cubits.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: he only has from the place
chunks.st: He has only

chunks.en: of his eiruv two thousand amos.
chunks.st: two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv, as the actual area of the city is included in the calculation.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva asks about an eiruv put in a cave. The Sages answer that if people live in the cave, the whole cave counts like four amos. The 2000 amos still end even in the middle of a cave.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to the Rabbis:

chunks.en: Don't you agree with me
chunks.st: Do you not concede to me

chunks.en: about one who puts his eiruv in a cave,
chunks.st: that one who places his eiruv in a cave

chunks.en: that he has from the place of his eiruv
chunks.st: has only

chunks.en: only two thousand amos?
chunks.st: two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv,
chunks.stMore: and that consequently the entire cave is not considered as merely four cubits?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: When is that? When no people live in it.
chunks.st: When does this apply? When the cave has no residents.

chunks.en: But if people live in it,
chunks.st: But if it has residents,
chunks.stMore: it is considered as though it were only four cubits, and

chunks.en: he may walk all of it and outside
chunks.st: one may walk through all of it and

chunks.en: of it two thousand amos.
chunks.st: another two thousand cubits beyond it.

chunks.en: So it turns out: inside it is easier than on top of it.
chunks.st: Consequently, the halakha with regard to an eiruv placed inside a cave is sometimes more lenient than the halakha governing an eiruv placed in the area above the cave.
chunks.stMore: If one places his eiruv inside a cave that has residents, he has two thousand cubits beyond the cave; if he places it above the cave, where there are no residents, he has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv.

chunks.en: And for the one measuring, who they said gets two thousand amos,
chunks.st: And as for one who is measuring his Shabbat limit, with regard to whom the Sages said that one gives him two thousand cubits,

chunks.en: even if his measuring ends inside a cave, it stops there.
chunks.st: that measurement applies even if the end of his measurement terminates in the middle of a cave. He may not walk further into the cave, even if the cave is inhabited.

mishnayos.summary: A Jew who shares a courtyard with a non-Jew, or with someone who does not believe in eiruv, may not carry there unless he rents that person's share. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says this is only when two Jews live there.

chunks.en: Someone who lives with a non-Jew in a courtyard,
chunks.st: One who resides with a gentile in the same courtyard,

chunks.he: אוֹ עִם מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָעֵרוּב,
chunks.en: or with someone who does not believe in eiruv,
chunks.st: or one who lives in the same courtyard with one who does not accept the principle of eiruv,
chunks.stMore: even though he is not a gentile, such as a Samaritan [Kuti],

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
chunks.en: that person makes it forbidden for him, says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this person renders it prohibited for him
chunks.stMore: to carry from his own house into the courtyard or from the courtyard into his house, unless he rents this person’s rights in the courtyard, as will be explained below.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.he: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵי
chunks.en: he never forbids unless there are two
chunks.st: Actually, the gentile does not render it prohibited for one to carry, unless there are two Jews

chunks.en: Jews who would forbid each other.
chunks.st: living in the same courtyard who themselves would prohibit one another from carrying if there were no eiruv. In such a case, the presence of the gentile renders the eiruv ineffective. However, if only one Jew lives there, the gentile does not render it prohibited for him to carry in the courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel tells about a Tzeduki who lived in their alleyway in Yerushalayim, and what his father told them to do so that the Tzeduki would not make the alleyway forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: there was a story with a Tzeduki
chunks.st: There was an incident involving a certain Sadducee

words.note: A Tzeduki did not believe in the teachings of the Sages.

chunks.en: who lived with us in an alleyway in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: who lived with us in the same alleyway in Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: who renounced his rights to the alleyway before Shabbat.

chunks.en: and Father said to us,
chunks.st: And Father said to us:

chunks.he: מַהֲרוּ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת כָּל הַכֵּלִים לַמָּבוֹי,
chunks.en: Hurry and take out all the things into the alleyway,
chunks.st: Hurry and take out your utensils to the alleyway
chunks.stMore: to establish possession of it,

chunks.en: before he takes out his things and makes it forbidden for you.
chunks.st: before he changes his mind and takes out
chunks.stMore: his own utensils so as to reclaim his rights, in which case he would render it prohibited for you to use the entire alleyway.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says it in a different way,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Rabban Gamliel’s father spoke to them with a different formulation,

chunks.en: Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway before
chunks.st: saying: Hurry and do whatever you must do in the alleyway
chunks.stMore: prior to Shabbat,

chunks.en: he takes out his things and makes it forbidden for you.
chunks.st: before he takes out his utensils and renders it prohibited for you to use the alleyway. In other words, you may not bring out utensils to the alleyway at all on Shabbat, as the institution of an eiruv cannot be used in the neighborhood of a Sadducee. This is because, even if he renounced his rights to the alleyway, he can always retract and reclaim them.

mishnayos.summary: If one person in a courtyard forgot to join the eiruv, his house may not be used for carrying, but the others' houses may. The mishnah also teaches what happens when the others give him their share, and when two people forgot.

chunks.he: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַד מֵהֶן וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: If one of the people of a courtyard forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one of the residents of a courtyard forgot and did not participate in an eiruv
chunks.stMore: with the other residents before Shabbat, and on Shabbat he renounced his rights in the courtyard to the other residents,

chunks.en: his house is forbidden for bringing things in and taking things out,
chunks.st: his house is prohibited both to him, who forgot to establish an eiruv, and to them, the other residents, to bring in objects from the courtyard to his house or to take them out
chunks.stMore: from his house into the courtyard.

chunks.en: for him and for them.
chunks.st: But their houses

chunks.en: But their houses are allowed,
chunks.st: are permitted

chunks.en: for him and for them.
chunks.st: both to him and to them,
chunks.stMore: for taking objects out into the courtyard and for bringing them in.

chunks.en: If they gave him their share,
chunks.st: If they gave away their rights in the courtyard to him, i.e., if they renounced their rights in his favor,

chunks.en: he is allowed and they are forbidden.
chunks.st: he is permitted to carry from his house into the courtyard, but they are prohibited
chunks.stMore: from doing so.

chunks.en: If there were two who forgot,
chunks.st: If two
chunks.stMore: residents of the courtyard forgot to establish an eiruv, and the others renounced their rights in the courtyard in their favor,

chunks.en: they forbid each other,
chunks.st: they prohibit one another.
chunks.stMore: In this scenario, the courtyard would belong to both of them, but each individual house remains the domain of its owner. It would therefore be prohibited for each of these residents to carry into the courtyard.

chunks.en: because one person can give a share and take a share,
chunks.st: For one resident may give away and receive rights
chunks.stMore: in a domain,

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם נוֹתְנִים רְשׁוּת וְאֵין נוֹטְלִין רְשׁוּת:
chunks.en: but two can give a share and cannot take a share.
chunks.st: whereas two residents may only give away rights in a domain, but they may not receive rights in a domain. Since they did not establish an eiruv, it is unreasonable for the other residents of the courtyard to give away their rights in the domain, as the two who are prohibited because they did not participate in the eiruv render it prohibited for each other to carry.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue when a person may give away his share in the courtyard. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue about someone who gave his share away and then carried out by mistake.

chunks.en: From when may we give away our share?
chunks.st: The mishna poses a general question: When may one give away rights in a domain?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: while it is still day.
chunks.st: While it is still day,
chunks.stMore: i.e., before the onset of Shabbat;

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even after dark. Someone who gave away his share and then carried out,
chunks.st: Even after nightfall, when it is already Shabbat. The mishna cites another dispute: If one gave away his rights in his courtyard to the other residents of the courtyard, renouncing them after having forgotten to establish an eiruv with them the previous day, and then he carried something out
chunks.stMore: from his house into the courtyard –

chunks.en: whether by mistake or on purpose,
chunks.st: whether unwittingly, forgetting that he had renounced his rights, or intentionally,

chunks.en: makes it forbidden,
chunks.st: he renders carrying prohibited
chunks.stMore: for all the residents of the courtyard, for his action cancels his renunciation;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: on purpose, he makes it forbidden;
chunks.st: If he acted intentionally, he renders carrying prohibited;

chunks.en: by mistake, he does not make it forbidden.
chunks.st: but if he acted unwittingly, he does not render carrying prohibited.

mishnayos.summary: If a homeowner shares wine with each of his neighbors, they do not need an eiruv. If he shares wine with one and oil with another, they do need one. Rabbi Shimon says they never need one.

chunks.en: A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors,
chunks.st: If a homeowner was in partnership with his neighbors,

chunks.en: with this one in wine and with that one in wine,
chunks.st: with this one in wine and with that one in wine,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they need not establish an eiruv,
chunks.stMore: for due to their authentic partnership they are considered to be one household, and no further partnership is required.

chunks.en: With this one in wine and that one in oil,
chunks.st: If, however, he was in partnership with this one in wine and with that one in oil,

chunks.en: they need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they must establish an eiruv.
chunks.stMore: As they are not partners in the same item, they are not all considered one partnership.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: both in this case and in that one,
chunks.st: In both this case and that case,
chunks.stMore: i.e., even if he partners with his neighbors in different items,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they need not establish an eiruv.

mishnayos.summary: Five groups stayed for Shabbos in one big hall split into parts. Beis Shammai say each group needs its own eiruv; Beis Hillel say one is enough, unless some are in separate rooms.

chunks.en: Five groups that spent Shabbos in one big hall,
chunks.st: With regard to five groups of people who spent Shabbat in one hall [teraklin]
chunks.stMore: that was subdivided by partitions into separate rooms, each of which had a separate entrance to a courtyard that was shared with other houses,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: an eiruv is needed for each and every group.
chunks.st: An eiruv is required for each and every group,
chunks.stMore: i.e., each group must contribute separately to the eiruv of the courtyard, as each is considered a different house.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: one eiruv for all of them.
chunks.st: One eiruv suffices for all of them,
chunks.stMore: as the partitions do not render the different sections separate houses.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן שְׁרוּיִן בַּחֲדָרִים אוֹ בַעֲלִיּוֹת,
chunks.en: And they agree that when some of them stay in rooms or upstairs rooms,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel concede that when some of them occupy separate rooms or upper stories,

chunks.he: שֶׁהֵן צְרִיכִין עֵרוּב לְכָל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה:
chunks.en: they need an eiruv for each and every group.
chunks.st: they require a separate eiruv for each and every group, and the fact that they are in the same building does not render them one unified group.

mishnayos.summary: Brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own houses each need to join the eiruv, unless the eiruv is in their father's house or nobody else lives in the courtyard.

chunks.en: Brothers who are partners, who eat at
chunks.st: In the case of brothers who were eating at their father’s table

chunks.en: their father's table and sleep in their own houses,
chunks.st: and sleeping in their own houses
chunks.stMore: in the same courtyard,

chunks.en: need an eiruv for each and every one.
chunks.st: a separate contribution to the eiruv is required for each and every one
chunks.stMore: of them.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם שָׁכַח אֶחָד מֵהֶם וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: So if one of them forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: Therefore, if one of them forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: he gives up his share.
chunks.st: he must renounce his rights
chunks.stMore: in the courtyard in order to render carrying in the courtyard permitted to the rest of the courtyard’s residents.

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין עֵרוּבָן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
chunks.en: When is this? When they take their eiruv to another place.
chunks.st: When do they state this halakha? They state it when they take their eiruv elsewhere
chunks.stMore: in the courtyard, i.e., to the house of one of the other residents.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵרוּב בָּא אֶצְלָן,
chunks.en: But if the eiruv was coming to them,
chunks.st: But if the eiruv was coming to them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if it was placed in their father’s house,

chunks.en: or there are no other people living with them in the courtyard,
chunks.st: or if there are no other residents with the brothers and their father in the courtyard,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they are not required to establish an eiruv, as they are considered like a single individual living in a courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: Five courtyards open into each other and into an alleyway. The mishnah teaches when they may carry in the courtyards and when in the alleyway, depending on the eiruv and the shituf.

chunks.en: Five courtyards that open one
chunks.st: If five courtyards open into one another and

chunks.en: into the next, and open into an alleyway,
chunks.st: also open into an alleyway,
chunks.stMore: the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if they made an eiruv in the courtyards but did not make a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: If the residents of the courtyard established an eiruv in the courtyards and did not merge the courtyards that open into the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry in the courtyards but not in the alleyway.
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and they are prohibited to carry in the alleyway.
chunks.stMore: The eiruv they established cannot also serve as a merging of the courtyards that open into the alleyway.

chunks.en: And if they made a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: And if they merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry here and there.
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry both here, in the alleyway, and there, in the courtyards.

chunks.en: If they made an eiruv in the courtyards and a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: If they established an eiruv in the courtyards and also merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

chunks.he: וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: and one of the courtyard people forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: and one of the residents of the courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv in his courtyard, but did participate in the merging of the courtyards in the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry here and there.
chunks.st: they are permitted both here and there,
chunks.stMore: as the merging of courtyards in the alleyway serves as an effective eiruv for the courtyards as well.

chunks.en: If one of the alleyway people did not join the shituf,
chunks.st: However, if one of the residents of the alleyway forgot and did not participate in the merging of courtyards that open into the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry in the courtyards but not in the alleyway,
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and prohibited from carrying in the alleyway,

chunks.en: because an alleyway to its courtyards is like a courtyard to its houses.
chunks.st: as the principle is: An alleyway is to its courtyards as a courtyard is to its houses.

mishnayos.summary: Two courtyards, one behind the other: the people of the inner one must walk through the outer one. The mishnah teaches which courtyard is allowed when one or both made an eiruv.

chunks.en: Two courtyards,
chunks.st: With regard to two courtyards,

chunks.en: one inside the other,
chunks.st: one of which was within the other,
chunks.stMore: and the outer one opened into the public domain, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if the inner one made an eiruv and the outer one did not,
chunks.st: If the inner courtyard established an eiruv for itself and the outer one did not establish an eiruv,

chunks.en: the inner one is allowed and the outer one is forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in the inner one is permitted and carrying in the outer one is prohibited.

chunks.en: If the outer one did, and not the inner one,
chunks.st: If the outer courtyard established an eiruv and the inner one did not,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in both is prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as the residents of the inner courtyard pass through the outer one, and are considered to a certain extent as residents of the courtyard who did not participate in the eiruv.

chunks.en: If this one made an eiruv for itself and that one for itself,
chunks.st: If this courtyard established an eiruv for itself,
chunks.stMore: and that courtyard also established an eiruv for itself, but they did not establish a joint eiruv with one another,

chunks.en: this one is allowed by itself,
chunks.st: this one is permitted by itself,

chunks.en: and that one is allowed by itself.
chunks.st: and that one is permitted by itself,
chunks.stMore: but they may not carry from one to the other.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva forbids the outer one,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva prohibits carrying in the outer one
chunks.stMore: even in such a case,

chunks.en: because the walking through it makes it forbidden.
chunks.st: as the right of entry to the outer courtyard enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard renders it prohibited.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis disagree and say:

chunks.en: walking through does not make it forbidden.
chunks.st: The right of entry enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard does not render it prohibited. Since the residents of the inner courtyard do not use the outer one other than to pass through it, and they are permitted to carry in their own courtyard, they do not render it prohibited to carry in the outer courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: More cases of an inner and outer courtyard: what happens if one person from either courtyard forgot to join the eiruv, and when no eiruv is needed at all.

chunks.he: שָׁכַח אַחַד מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: If one from the outer courtyard forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one resident of the outer courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: the inner one is allowed and the outer one is forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in the inner courtyard is permitted and in the outer one is prohibited.

chunks.en: If one from the inner one did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one resident of the inner courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: they are both prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as the right of way enjoyed by the members of the inner courtyard through the outer courtyard renders the outer one prohibited as well.

chunks.en: If they put their eiruv in one place,
chunks.st: If the residents of both courtyards put their eiruv in one place,

chunks.en: and one person forgot,
chunks.st: and one person,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הַפְּנִימִית בֵּין מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה,
chunks.en: whether from the inner one or from the outer one,
chunks.st: whether he was from the inner courtyard or from the outer one,

chunks.en: and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: they are both prohibited
chunks.stMore: for carrying within them, as the two courtyards are treated as one.

chunks.en: And if they belonged to single people,
chunks.st: And if the courtyards belonged to individuals,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if only one person lived in each courtyard,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they are not required to establish an eiruv, as this requirement applies only to a courtyard occupied by multiple residents.

mishnayos.summary: Two courtyards with a big enough, low enough window between them may make one eiruv together or two separate ones. If the window is too small or too high, each must make its own.

chunks.en: A window between two courtyards,
chunks.st: If there is a window in a wall that separates between two courtyards,

chunks.en: four tefachim by four,
chunks.st: and the window measures four by four

chunks.en: within ten tefachim of the ground,
chunks.st: handbreadths and is within ten handbreadths of the ground,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin,
chunks.st: the inhabitants of the courtyards establish two eiruvin,
chunks.stMore: one for each courtyard.

chunks.en: and if they want,
chunks.st: And if they desire, they

chunks.en: they make one eiruv.
chunks.st: may establish one eiruv,
chunks.stMore: thereby merging the two courtyards, as they may be considered as one due to the window.

chunks.en: Less than four by four,
chunks.st: However, if the window measures less than four by four

chunks.en: or higher than ten,
chunks.st: handbreadths, or if it is above ten
chunks.stMore: handbreadths from the ground, it is no longer considered a valid opening, and the two courtyards cannot be considered a single courtyard.

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin and may not make one.
chunks.st: Therefore, the residents establish two eiruvin, but they may not establish one eiruv.

mishnayos.summary: A tall, wide wall between two courtyards keeps them apart, so each makes its own eiruv. Both sides may eat fruit on top of it. If the wall breaks, it depends on how wide the gap is.

chunks.en: A wall between two courtyards
chunks.st: If a wall between two courtyards

chunks.en: ten tefachim tall and four wide,
chunks.st: is ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin and may not make one.
chunks.st: the residents of the courtyard establish two eiruvin, a separate one for each courtyard, but they may not establish one eiruv.

chunks.en: If there was fruit on top of it,
chunks.st: If there was produce on top of the wall,

chunks.en: these go up from here and eat,
chunks.st: these residents of one courtyard may ascend from this side and eat from it,

chunks.en: and those go up from there and eat,
chunks.st: and those residents of the other courtyard may ascend from that side and eat from it,

chunks.en: as long as they do not bring it down.
chunks.st: provided that they do not lower the produce down from on top of the wall to one of the courtyards.

chunks.en: If the wall broke open up to ten amos,
chunks.st: If the wall was breached, the following distinction applies: If the breach was up to ten cubits wide,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin,
chunks.st: they establish two eiruvin,

chunks.en: and if they want, they make one,
chunks.st: and if they desire, they may establish one eiruv,

chunks.en: because it is like a doorway.
chunks.st: as it is similar to an entrance,
chunks.stMore: like any opening less than ten cubits wide.

chunks.en: More than that,
chunks.st: If the breach was more than this,

chunks.en: they make one eiruv and may not make two.
chunks.st: they establish one eiruv, and they may not establish two, as a breach of this size nullifies the partition and joins the two courtyards into a single domain.

mishnayos.summary: A deep, wide ditch between two courtyards keeps them apart, even if it is filled with straw. If it is filled with dirt or stones, it is as if it is not there.

chunks.en: A ditch between two courtyards
chunks.st: With regard to a ditch between two courtyards

chunks.en: ten tefachim deep and four wide,
chunks.st: that is ten handbreadths deep and four handbreadths wide,
chunks.stMore: it is considered a full-fledged partition, and

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin and may not make one,
chunks.st: the residents of the courtyard establish two eiruvin, one for each courtyard, but they may not establish one eiruv.

chunks.en: even if it is full of straw or hay.
chunks.st: Even if the ditch is filled with straw or hay,
chunks.stMore: it is not regarded as sealed and is therefore not nullified. However,

chunks.en: If it is full of dirt,
chunks.st: if the ditch is filled with dirt

chunks.en: or pebbles,
chunks.st: or pebbles,

chunks.en: they make one eiruv,
chunks.st: the residents establish one eiruv,

chunks.en: and may not make two.
chunks.st: but they may not establish two eiruvin, as the ditch is nullified and considered nonexistent.

mishnayos.summary: If a board four tefachim wide is put across the ditch, or between two balconies, the courtyards may make one eiruv together if they want. A thinner board does not join them.

chunks.en: If he put on it a board that is
chunks.st: If one placed a board four handbreadths wide across the ditch

chunks.en: four tefachim wide,
chunks.st: so that he could cross it,

chunks.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזֻזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ,
chunks.en: and also two balconies across from each other,
chunks.st: and similarly, if two balconies [gezuztraot] in two different courtyards are opposite one another,
chunks.stMore: and one placed a board four handbreadths wide between them,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin,
chunks.st: the residents of the courtyards or balconies establish two eiruvin,

chunks.en: and if they want,
chunks.st: and if they desire, they

chunks.en: they make one eiruv.
chunks.st: may establish one,
chunks.stMore: as the board serves as an opening and a passageway between them.

chunks.en: If less than that,
chunks.st: If the width of the plank is less than four handbreadths,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin and may not make one.
chunks.st: the residents establish two eiruvin, but they may not establish one eiruv.

mishnayos.summary: A pile of hay ten tefachim tall between two courtyards is like a wall. Both sides may feed their animals from it. If the hay gets lower than ten tefachim, they make one eiruv.

chunks.en: A pile of hay between two courtyards,
chunks.st: With regard to a haystack that is positioned between two courtyards

chunks.en: ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: and is ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: it has the status of a partition,

chunks.en: they make two eiruvin and may not make one.
chunks.st: and therefore the residents of the courtyards may establish two eiruvin, and they may not establish one eiruv.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן וְאֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן.
chunks.en: These feed their animals from here, and those feed from there.
chunks.st: These, the inhabitants of one courtyard, may feed their animals from here, from one side of the haystack, and those, the inhabitants of the other courtyard, may feed their animals from there, from the other side of the haystack.
chunks.stMore: There is no concern that the haystack might become too small to serve as a partition.

chunks.en: If the hay became lower than ten tefachim,
chunks.st: If the height of the hay was reduced to less than ten handbreadths
chunks.stMore: across its entire length, its legal status is no longer that of a partition. Consequently,

chunks.en: they make one eiruv and may not make two.
chunks.st: the residents of both courtyards establish one eiruv, and they do not establish two eiruvin.

mishnayos.summary: How does one person make a shituf for everyone in the alleyway? He puts down a barrel of his food and gives it to them through someone else who can take it for them.

chunks.en: How do we make a shituf in an alleyway?
chunks.st: How does one merge the courtyards that open into the alleyway,
chunks.stMore: if a person wishes to act on behalf of all the residents of the alleyway?

chunks.en: He puts down the barrel and says,
chunks.st: He places a barrel filled with his own food and says:

chunks.en: This is for all the people of the alleyway.
chunks.st: This is for all the residents of the alleyway.
chunks.stMore: For this gift to be acquired by the others, someone must accept it on their behalf,

chunks.en: And he gives it to them through his son
chunks.st: and the tanna therefore teaches that he may confer possession to them

chunks.en: and daughter who are grown up, and through his servant
chunks.st: even by means of his adult son or daughter, and

chunks.en: and maid who are Jewish, and through his wife.
chunks.st: likewise by means of his Hebrew slave or maidservant, whom he does not own, and by means of his wife.
chunks.stMore: These people may acquire the eiruv on behalf of all the residents of the alleyway.

chunks.en: But he may not give it to them
chunks.st: However, he may not confer possession

chunks.en: through his son and daughter who are young, nor
chunks.st: by means of his minor son or daughter, nor

chunks.en: through his non-Jewish servant and maid,
chunks.st: by means of his Canaanite slave or maidservant,

chunks.en: because their hand is like his hand.
chunks.explain: What they get belongs to him, so it is as if he never gave it away.
chunks.st: because they cannot effect acquisition, as ownership of objects that come into their possession is as if those objects came into his possession. Consequently, the master or father cannot confer possession to the slave or minor respectively on behalf of others as their acquisition is ineffective and the object remains in his own possession.

mishnayos.summary: If the food of the shituf gets used up, he may add more without telling anyone. If new people move in, he adds for them and must tell them.

chunks.en: If the food became less,
chunks.st: If the food in the barrel for the merging of the alleyway diminished
chunks.stMore: and was less than the requisite measure,

chunks.en: he adds more and gives it to them,
chunks.st: one may add a little of his own and confer possession

chunks.en: and he does not need to tell them.
chunks.st: to the others, and he need not inform
chunks.stMore: them of his addition. However,

chunks.en: If more people were added to them,
chunks.st: if new residents were added to

chunks.en: he adds more and gives it to them,
chunks.st: the residents of the alleyway, he may add food on behalf of those residents and confer possession

chunks.en: and he must tell them.
chunks.st: to them, and he must inform the new residents of their inclusion in the merging of alleyways.

mishnayos.summary: How much food is needed for the shituf? If there are many people, food for two meals is enough for all; if few, a dried fig's size for each person.

chunks.en: How much must it be?
chunks.st: What is the measure
chunks.stMore: of food required for a merging of the alleyways?

chunks.en: When there are many people,
chunks.st: When the residents of the alley are numerous,

chunks.en: food for two meals for all of them.
chunks.st: food for two meals is sufficient for all of them;

chunks.en: When there are few,
chunks.st: when they are few,
chunks.stMore: less than a certain number,

chunks.he: כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת לְהוֹצָאַת שַׁבָּת לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:
chunks.en: the size of a dried fig for each and every one.
chunks.explain: The same small amount that is counted for carrying on Shabbos.
chunks.st: a dried fig-bulk for each and every one of them is enough.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosi says the amounts are only needed at the start; what is left of an eiruv works even if it is tiny. The eiruv for courtyards was kept so children would not forget about eiruv.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: when does this apply?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: At the start of an eiruv.
chunks.st: It is said with regard to the beginning of an eiruv,

chunks.en: But for what is left of an eiruv,
chunks.st: However, with regard to the remnants of an eiruv,

chunks.st: it remains valid if even any amount

chunks.en: And they only said to make an eiruv for courtyards
chunks.st: remains. And in general they said that it is necessary to join the courtyards,
chunks.stMore: even though a merging of the alleyways was already in place,

chunks.en: so that the children will not forget about it.
chunks.st: only so that the halakhic category of eiruv will not be forgotten by the children, i.e., so that the next generation should be aware that an eiruv can be established for a courtyard, for otherwise they would be entirely unaware of this halakhic category.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer says an eiruv may be made with any food except water and salt. Rabbi Yehoshua says it must be a whole loaf; even a small whole loaf works, but a big loaf in pieces does not.

chunks.en: We may make an eiruv and a shituf with any food,
chunks.st: One may join courtyards and merge alleyways with all types of food,

chunks.en: except water and salt,
chunks.st: except for water and salt,
chunks.stMore: as they are not considered foods.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says
chunks.stMore: that a different limitation applies: A whole

chunks.en: a loaf is an eiruv.
chunks.st: loaf may be used for an eiruv.

chunks.en: Even a baked loaf as big as a se'ah, if it is in pieces,
chunks.st: With regard to a baked product even the size of a se’a, if it consists of pieces,

words.note: A se'ah is a big measure of flour.

chunks.en: we may not make an eiruv with it.
chunks.st: one may not join courtyards with it.

chunks.en: A loaf worth just an issar, if it is whole,
chunks.st: However, with regard to a loaf, even one the size of an issar, if it is whole,

words.note: An issar is a small coin.

chunks.en: we may make an eiruv with it.
chunks.st: one may join courtyards with it.

mishnayos.summary: May a person pay a storekeeper so that he will get a share in the eiruv? The Rabbis argue. Rabbi Yehudah says a courtyard eiruv may be made for someone without asking him, because it only helps him.

chunks.en: A person may give a coin to a storekeeper or a baker
chunks.st: A person may give a ma’a coin to a grocer or a baker,
chunks.stMore: if they live in the same alleyway or courtyard,

chunks.en: so that he will get a share in the eiruv for him,
chunks.st: so that the grocer or baker will confer upon him possession of wine or bread for a merging of the alleyway or an eiruv,
chunks.stMore: if other residents come to them to purchase these products for that purpose.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: his money did not get it for him.
chunks.st: His money did not confer possession on him,
chunks.stMore: as the transfer of money alone is not a valid mode of acquisition and cannot confer possession. One must perform a valid mode of acquisition, e.g., pulling an article into one’s possession, to transfer ownership.

chunks.en: And they agree about all other people
chunks.st: And the Rabbis concede with regard to all other people,
chunks.stMore: apart from grocers and bakers,

chunks.en: that his money does get it for him,
chunks.st: that if one gave them money for the food of an eiruv, his money confers possession upon him,

chunks.en: because we only make an eiruv for a person when he knows.
chunks.st: as one may establish an eiruv for a person only with his knowledge
chunks.stMore: and at his bidding. With regard to a grocer or baker, the person giving the money does not intend to appoint the grocer or the baker as his agent and the money itself does not effect an acquisition, and consequently, he did not accomplish anything. With regard to anyone else, however, there is no doubt that he must have intended to appoint him his agent, and his act is effective.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: when does this apply?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: For an eiruv techumin.
chunks.st: It is said with regard to a joining of Shabbat boundaries,

chunks.en: But for an eiruv for courtyards,
chunks.st: but with regard to a joining of courtyards, one

chunks.en: we may make it for him whether he knows or not,
chunks.st: may establish an eiruv for a person either with his knowledge or without his knowledge.

chunks.en: because we may do something good for a person when he is not there,
chunks.st: The reason is because one may act for a person’s benefit in his absence,

chunks.en: but we may not do something bad for a person when he is not there.
chunks.explain: An eiruv techumin lets him walk one way but takes away the other way.
chunks.st: but one may not act to a person’s disadvantage in his absence. As a participant in a joining of courtyards benefits from his inclusion in the eiruv, his consent is not required. However, with regard to a joining of Shabbat boundaries, although it enables one to go farther in one direction, he loses the option of traveling in the opposite direction. When an action is to a person’s disadvantage, or if it entails both benefits and disadvantages, one may act on that person’s behalf only if he has been explicitly appointed his agent.

mishnayos.summary: One person can make an eiruv techumin for everyone in his town who wants to walk far on Shabbos to comfort mourners or go to a wedding. Only those who agreed before Shabbos may use it.

chunks.en: How do we make a shituf for the Shabbos limits?
chunks.st: How does one participate in the joining of Shabbat boundaries?

chunks.en: He puts down the barrel and says,
chunks.st: One who wishes to establish a joining of Shabbat boundaries for himself and others places a barrel of food in the location he designates as their place of residence, and says:

chunks.en: This is for all the people of my town,
chunks.st: This is for all the residents of my town,

chunks.en: for anyone who will go to a house
chunks.st: for anyone who wishes to go

chunks.en: of mourning or to a wedding party.
chunks.st: on Shabbat to a house of mourning or to a house of a wedding feast situated beyond the Shabbat limit.

chunks.en: Anyone who agreed to it while it was still day
chunks.st: Anyone who accepted upon himself while it was still day,
chunks.stMore: i.e., before the onset of Shabbat, that he will rely on the eiruv,

chunks.en: is allowed. After dark,
chunks.st: is permitted to rely upon it; but if one did so only after nightfall,

chunks.en: he is forbidden, because we do not make an eiruv after dark.
chunks.st: he is prohibited to rely upon it, as the principle is that one may not establish an eiruv after nightfall.

mishnayos.summary: An eiruv techumin needs enough food for two meals for each person. The Rabbis argue how big a meal is. The mishnah also uses the same loaf to measure other halachos.

chunks.en: How much must it be?
chunks.st: What is the measure
chunks.stMore: for an joining of Shabbat boundaries?

chunks.en: Food for two meals for each person.
chunks.st: It consists of a quantity of food sufficient for two meals for each and every one
chunks.stMore: of those included in the eiruv. The tanna’im disagree with regard to the size of these two meals.

chunks.en: The food he eats on a weekday, not on Shabbos,
chunks.st: It is referring to one’s food that he eats on a weekday and not on Shabbat;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: for Shabbos, not for a weekday.
chunks.st: It is referring to the amount he eats on Shabbat and not on a weekday.

chunks.en: And both of them mean to make it easier.
chunks.st: And both this Sage, Rabbi Meir, and that Sage, Rabbi Yehuda, intended to be lenient,
chunks.stMore: as Rabbi Meir maintains that people eat more food on Shabbat, whereas Rabbi Yehuda believes that they consume more on a weekday.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

chunks.en: a loaf bought for a pundyon,
chunks.st: Food for two meals is the size of a loaf bought with a pundeyon,
chunks.stMore: which is one-forty-eighth of a sela,

words.note: A small coin.

chunks.en: when wheat costs four se'ah for a sela.
chunks.st: when four se’a of wheat are sold for a sela.

words.note: A bigger coin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: two parts of a loaf, when three loaves are made from a kav.
chunks.st: Food for two meals is two of three parts of a loaf, when three loaves are prepared from a kav
chunks.stMore: of wheat. In other words, the measure is two-thirds of a loaf the size of one-third of a kav.

words.note: A kav is a measure of flour.

chunks.en: Half of it is for a house with tzaraas,
chunks.explain: Staying that long inside makes his clothes tamei.
chunks.st: Having discussed measures with regard to a loaf of bread, the mishna states that half of this loaf is the amount called a half [peras], a measure relevant for the halakhot of a leprous house.
chunks.stMore: If one enters a house afflicted with leprosy and remains there long enough to eat this amount of food, the clothes he is wearing become ritually impure.

words.note: A sickness sign that can appear on the walls of a house.

chunks.en: and half of its half makes the body unfit for terumah.
chunks.st: And half of its half, a quarter of this loaf, is the amount of ritually impure food that disqualifies the body.
chunks.stMore: In other words, impure food of this amount imparts ritual impurity to the body of the eater, and disqualifies him by rabbinic law from eating teruma.

mishnayos.summary: When the people of a courtyard and the people of a balcony above it did not make an eiruv together, the mishnah teaches which tall things in the courtyard belong to the balcony and which belong to the courtyard.

chunks.en: People of a courtyard and people of a balcony
chunks.st: If both the residents of houses that open directly into a courtyard and the residents of apartments that open onto a balcony
chunks.stMore: from which stairs lead down to that courtyard

chunks.en: who forgot and did not make an eiruv together,
chunks.st: forgot and did not establish an eiruv
chunks.stMore: between them,

chunks.en: anything ten tefachim tall
chunks.st: anything in the courtyard that is ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: e.g., a mound or a post,

chunks.en: belongs to the balcony. Less than that,
chunks.st: is part of the balcony. The residents of the apartments open to the balcony may transfer objects to and from their apartments onto the mound or post. Any post or mound that is lower than this

chunks.en: belongs to the courtyard. The wall around a pit, or a rock,
chunks.st: height is part of the courtyard. A similar halakha applies to an embankment that surrounds a cistern or a rock:

chunks.en: if they are ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: If the embankments that surround a cistern or rock are ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: belong to the balcony. Less than that,
chunks.st: they belong to the balcony; if they are lower than this,

chunks.en: belong to the courtyard. When does this apply?
chunks.st: they may be used only by the inhabitants of the courtyard. In what case are these matters, the halakha that anything higher than ten handbreadths belongs to the balcony, stated?

chunks.en: When it is near. But if it is far away,
chunks.st: When the mound or embankment is near the balcony. But in a case where the embankment or mound is distant from it,

chunks.en: even if it is ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: even if it is ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: it belongs to the courtyard. And what is near?
chunks.st: the right to use the embankment or mound goes to the members of the courtyard. And what is considered near?

chunks.en: Anything that is not four tefachim away.
chunks.st: Anything that is not four handbreadths removed from the balcony.

mishnayos.summary: A courtyard eiruv must be put in a real room. An eiruv put in a gatehouse, porch or balcony does not work, but one in a hay shed, barn or storeroom does. The mishnah also teaches who living there makes carrying forbidden.

chunks.en: Someone who puts his eiruv in a gatehouse,
chunks.st: With regard to one who placed his eiruv of courtyards in a gatehouse

chunks.en: a porch, or a balcony,
chunks.st: or in a portico, a roofed structure without walls or with incomplete walls, or one who deposited it in a balcony,

words.note: A roof with no full walls.

chunks.en: it is not an eiruv.
chunks.st: this is not a valid eiruv.

chunks.en: And someone who lives there
chunks.st: And one who resides there,
chunks.stMore: in any of these structures,

chunks.en: does not make it forbidden for him.
chunks.st: does not render it prohibited
chunks.stMore: for the homeowner and the other residents of the courtyard to carry, even if he did not contribute to the eiruv.

chunks.en: In a hay shed, in a cow shed,
chunks.st: If, however, one deposited his eiruv in a hay shed or in a cowshed or

chunks.en: in a wood shed, or in a storeroom,
chunks.st: in a woodshed or in a storehouse,

chunks.en: it is an eiruv.
chunks.st: this is a valid eiruv,
chunks.stMore: as it is located in a properly guarded place.

chunks.en: And someone who lives there
chunks.st: And one who resides there

chunks.en: makes it forbidden for him.
chunks.st: with permission, if he neglected to contribute to the eiruv, he renders it prohibited
chunks.stMore: for the homeowner and the other residents of the courtyard to carry.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if there is a place there that is held
chunks.st: If the homeowner has there,
chunks.stMore: in the hay shed or the other places listed above,

chunks.en: by the homeowner,
chunks.st: a right of usage,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if he is entitled to use all or part of the area for his own purposes, then

chunks.en: he does not make it forbidden for him.
chunks.st: the one who lives there does not render it prohibited for the homeowner, as the area is considered the homeowner’s quarters, and the person living there is classified as a member of his household.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who left his house in a shared courtyard to spend Shabbos in another town: the Rabbis argue whether his empty house still makes carrying in the courtyard forbidden.

chunks.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ וְהָלַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּעִיר אַחֶרֶת,
chunks.en: Someone who leaves his house and goes to spend Shabbos in another town,
chunks.st: One who leaves his house, which is located in a shared courtyard, and goes to spend Shabbat in a different town,

chunks.en: whether he is a non-Jew or a Jew,
chunks.st: whether he is a gentile or a Jew,

chunks.en: makes it forbidden,
chunks.st: he renders it prohibited
chunks.stMore: for the other residents to use the courtyard as though he were still at home;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he does not make it forbidden.
chunks.st: He does not render it prohibited for them,
chunks.stMore: as he left behind him an empty residence.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: a non-Jew makes it forbidden,
chunks.st: A gentile renders it prohibited

chunks.en: a Jew does not make it forbidden,
chunks.st: but a Jew does not render it prohibited,

chunks.en: because a Jew does not usually come back on Shabbos.
chunks.st: as it is not the manner of a Jew to come home on Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: A Jew will not return home, therefore his empty residence does not render it prohibited. By contrast, a gentile might return over the course of Shabbat. Therefore, he is not considered to have fully uprooted himself from his house, and he renders it prohibited.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even if he left his house and went to spend Shabbos
chunks.st: Even if the Jew left his house and went to spend Shabbat

chunks.en: at his daughter's house in the same town,
chunks.st: with his daughter who lived in the same town,

chunks.en: he does not make it forbidden,
chunks.st: he does not render it prohibited.
chunks.stMore: Although he can return home at any time, it is assumed

chunks.en: because he already took it out of his mind.
chunks.st: that he has already removed from his mind any thought of going back there and has established his Shabbat residence away from his home.

mishnayos.summary: A water pit between two courtyards may not be used on Shabbos unless a wall divides it. The Rabbis argue where the wall must be, and Rabbi Yehudah says the wall over it is enough.

chunks.en: A pit between two courtyards,
chunks.st: In the case of a cistern that is located between two courtyards,
chunks.stMore: situated partly in each courtyard,

chunks.en: we may not take water from it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: one may not draw water from it on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: lest the residents of one courtyard draw water from the domain of the other courtyard,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לוֹ מְחִצָּה
chunks.en: unless they made a wall for it
chunks.st: unless a partition

chunks.en: ten tefachim tall, whether above,
chunks.st: ten handbreadths high was erected for it
chunks.stMore: as a separation between the domains.

chunks.en: or below,

chunks.st: or whether it is within the airspace of the cistern below the rim,
chunks.stMore: above the surface of the water.

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
chunks.stMore: This is the subject of an early dispute of tanna’im, as

chunks.st: Beit Shammai said

mishnayos.summary: A stream of water running through a courtyard may not be used on Shabbos unless it has walls where it comes in and goes out. Rabbi Yehudah says the wall above it is enough, and tells a story from the town of Avel.

chunks.en: A water stream that runs through a courtyard,
chunks.st: With regard to a water channel that passes through a courtyard,

chunks.en: we may not take water from it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: the residents may not draw water from it on Shabbat,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִצָּה
chunks.en: unless they made a wall for it
chunks.st: unless they erected for it a partition

chunks.en: ten tefachim tall where it comes in and where it goes out.
chunks.st: ten handbreadths high at the entrance and at the exit
chunks.stMore: of the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: There was a story with the stream of Avel, that they took water

chunks.en: from it on Shabbos because the elders said they could.
chunks.st: from it on Shabbat by the authority of the Elders,
chunks.stMore: relying on the courtyard wall suspended above it.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: that was because it was not big enough to need a wall.

mishnayos.summary: People on a balcony over water may not take up water through a hole on Shabbos unless they make a wall around it. If there are two balconies one above the other, both need it or they must make an eiruv.

chunks.en: A balcony that is above the water,
chunks.st: With regard to a balcony that extends over a body of water,
chunks.stMore: if a hole was opened in the floor,

chunks.en: we may not take water from it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: its residents may not draw water from it through the hole on Shabbat,

chunks.st: unless they erected for it

chunks.st: a partition ten handbreadths high

chunks.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזֻזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ.

chunks.st: And likewise, with regard to two such balconies, one above the other,

chunks.st: if they erected a partition for the upper balcony but they did not erect one for the lower one,

mishnayos.summary: In a very small courtyard, water may not be poured out on Shabbos unless there is a pit that can hold it, so it does not flow into the street.

chunks.en: A courtyard that is smaller than four amos,
chunks.st: With regard to a courtyard that is less than four cubits
chunks.stMore: by four cubits in area,

chunks.en: we may not pour water into it on Shabbos,
chunks.st: one may not pour waste water into it on Shabbat,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ עוּקָה
chunks.en: unless they made for it a pit
chunks.st: unless a pit was fashioned

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says water may be poured into a covered drain that goes out into the street. The Sages say we may not pour straight into the drain, but may let it flow there from the roof.

chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: a drain that is covered for four
