chunks.st: from which the water spills into the drain of its own accord.

chunks.en: A courtyard and a porch join together to make four amos.
chunks.st: A courtyard and a portico, a roofed but unwalled structure in front of a house, combine for the four cubits by virtue of which it is permitted to pour water even into a courtyard that lacks a pit.

mishnayos.summary: Two upstairs homes facing each other over a small courtyard: those who made a pit may pour out water, and those who did not make one may not.

chunks.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי דְיוֹטָאוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ,
chunks.en: And the same with two upstairs homes across from each other,
chunks.st: And likewise, with regard to two upper stories [deyotaot], one opposite the other
chunks.stMore: in the same small courtyard,

chunks.en: some of them made a pit and some
chunks.st: if the residents of one of them fashioned a pit
chunks.stMore: in the courtyard,

chunks.en: did not make a pit,
chunks.st: and the residents of the other did not fashion a pit,

chunks.en: those who made a pit
chunks.st: those who fashioned a pit

chunks.he: מֻתָּרִין, וְאֶת שֶׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ עוּקָה, אֲסוּרִין:
chunks.en: are allowed, and those who did not make a pit are forbidden.
chunks.st: are permitted to pour their waste water into the courtyard, whereas those who did not fashion a pit are prohibited to do so.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir says all the roofs of a city count as one area, so we may carry between them if they are about the same height. The Sages say each roof is its own area. Rabbi Shimon teaches about things that were already outside when Shabbos began.

chunks.en: All the roofs of the city
chunks.st: All the roofs of the city

chunks.en: are one area,
chunks.st: are considered one domain.
chunks.stMore: It is permitted to carry from one roof to another, even if the residents of the houses did not establish an eiruv between them. The Sages did not prohibit carrying between roofs, as it is rare to transfer an item from one roof to another.

chunks.en: as long as one roof is not ten tefachim higher
chunks.st: However, it is only permitted to transfer objects between roofs provided that one roof is neither ten handbreadths higher

chunks.en: or ten tefachim lower,
chunks.st: nor ten handbreadths lower than the adjacent roof.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
chunks.en: each and every one is an area by itself.
chunks.st: Each and every one of the roofs is a domain in and of itself.
chunks.stMore: It is permitted to carry from one to the other only if the residents of both houses established an eiruv.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: אֶחָד גַּגּוֹת וְאֶחָד חֲצֵרוֹת וְאֶחָד קַרְפֵּיפוֹת,
chunks.en: roofs, courtyards, and storage yards together
chunks.st: Roofs, courtyards, and enclosures

chunks.en: are one area for things that were inside them when Shabbos began,
chunks.st: are all one domain with regard to vessels that were inside them when Shabbat began,
chunks.stMore: and one may therefore carry from one of these areas to another.

chunks.en: but not for things that were inside the house when Shabbos began.
chunks.st: However, they are not one domain with regard to vessels that were inside the house when Shabbat began and were later taken into one of the above domains. A vessel that was inside the house when Shabbat began and subsequently carried to one of these areas may be carried from one roof, courtyard, or enclosure to another only if an eiruv had been established between the domains.

mishnayos.summary: A big roof or courtyard next to a small one may be used, but the small one may not. A courtyard that broke open to the street is argued about: Rabbi Eliezer says it becomes like the street, the Sages say it is a karmelis.

chunks.en: A big roof next to a small one,
chunks.st: If a large roof was adjacent to a small roof,
chunks.stMore: and the boundary between them was no wider than ten cubits,

chunks.en: the big one is allowed and the small one is forbidden.
chunks.st: use of the large one is permitted, i.e., one may bring objects up to the roof from the house below and carry them on the roof, and use of the small one is prohibited.

chunks.en: A big courtyard that broke open into a small one,
chunks.st: A similar halakha applies to a large courtyard that was breached into a small one,
chunks.stMore: in a manner that one entire side of the small courtyard was breached, but the breach was less than ten cubits;

chunks.en: the big one is allowed,
chunks.st: it is permitted for the residents of the large courtyard to carry,

chunks.en: and the small one is forbidden,
chunks.st: but it is prohibited for the residents of the small one to do so.

chunks.en: because the gap is like a doorway of the big one.
chunks.explain: For the big one, walls are left on both sides of the gap.
chunks.st: The rationale for this difference is because in that case, the legal status of the breach is like that of the entrance of the large courtyard.
chunks.stMore: As the breach in the wall of the larger courtyard is surrounded on both sides by the remaining portions of that wall, and the breach is no greater than ten cubits wide, its legal status is like that of an entrance in the wall of the courtyard, and therefore it is permitted to carry in the large courtyard. With regard to the small courtyard, however, since one entire side of the small courtyard was breached, there remains no partition whatsoever on that side and carrying in that courtyard is therefore prohibited.

chunks.en: A courtyard that broke open to the public street,
chunks.st: With regard to a courtyard that was breached into the public domain,
chunks.stMore: and the breach was more than ten cubits wide, so that it cannot be considered an entrance,

chunks.en: someone who brings something from it into a private area,
chunks.st: one who carries an object from inside the courtyard into the private domain,

chunks.en: or from a private area into it,
chunks.st: or from the private domain into it,

chunks.en: is chayav, says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.explain: Chayav means he broke a Torah law of Shabbos.
chunks.st: is liable, as it ceases to be a private domain and is subsumed into the public domain. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

words.note: Guilty of breaking a Torah law.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis disagree and say:

chunks.en: from it into the public street,
chunks.st: One who carries from inside the courtyard into the public domain,

chunks.en: or from the public street into it,
chunks.st: or from the public domain into it,

chunks.en: he is patur, because it is like a karmelis.
chunks.explain: A karmelis is an in-between area, forbidden only by the Rabbis.
chunks.st: is exempt, because its legal status is like that of a karmelit. Although it ceases to be a private domain, it does not become a full-fledged public domain.

words.note: Not guilty of breaking a Torah law.
An area that is not fully private or public.

mishnayos.summary: If a courtyard or house broke open on Shabbos, or an alleyway's korah or lechi was taken away, Rabbi Yehudah says we may carry there for the rest of that Shabbos only. Rabbi Yosi disagrees.

chunks.he: חָצֵר שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מִשְּׁתֵּי רוּחוֹתֶיהָ,
chunks.en: A courtyard that broke open to the public street on two sides,
chunks.st: With regard to a courtyard that was breached on Shabbat into a public domain from two of its sides,

chunks.en: and also a house that broke open on two sides,
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to a house that was breached from two of its sides,

chunks.he: וְכֵן מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ קוֹרוֹתָיו אוֹ לְחָיָיו,
chunks.en: and also an alleyway whose korah or lechi were taken away,
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to an alleyway whose cross beams or side posts were removed
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat,

chunks.he: מֻתָּרִין בְּאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת וַאֲסוּרִין לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,
chunks.en: are allowed on that Shabbos and forbidden in the future,
chunks.st: the residents of that domain are permitted to carry there on that Shabbat, but are prohibited from doing so in the future.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.stMore: This cannot be the halakha, as

chunks.en: if they are allowed on that Shabbos,
chunks.st: if they are permitted to carry there on that Shabbat,

chunks.en: they are allowed in the future.
chunks.st: they are likewise permitted to do so in the future,

chunks.en: And if they are forbidden in the future,
chunks.st: and if they are prohibited from carrying there in the future,

chunks.en: they are forbidden on that Shabbos.
chunks.st: they are also prohibited from carrying there on that Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah says we may carry under a room built across two houses or under a bridge, and that an alleyway open on both ends can have an eiruv. The Sages forbid both.

chunks.he: הַבּוֹנֶה עֲלִיָּה עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים,
chunks.en: Someone who builds an upstairs room on top of two houses,
chunks.st: With regard to one who builds an upper story atop two houses
chunks.stMore: on opposite sides of a public domain that passes beneath it,

chunks.en: and also bridges that are open on both ends,
chunks.st: and likewise bridges with a thoroughfare
chunks.stMore: beneath them that rest on walls on opposite sides of a public domain,

chunks.en: we may carry under them on Shabbos,
chunks.st: one may carry beneath the upper story and beneath the bridge on Shabbat.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,
chunks.stMore: who maintains that these areas are considered private domains.

chunks.en: And the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis prohibit
chunks.stMore: carrying in these areas.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehudah also said,
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: we may make an eiruv for an alleyway open on both ends.
chunks.st: One may establish an eiruv even for an alleyway that is open
chunks.stMore: at both ends, with no need for any additional measures,

chunks.en: And the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis prohibit doing so.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who finds tefillin outside on Shabbos may bring them in by wearing them, one pair at a time. The mishnah teaches what to do with new tefillin, with a big bundle, and when it is dangerous.

chunks.en: Someone who finds tefillin
chunks.st: One who finds phylacteries
chunks.stMore: outside the city on Shabbat, where they are in danger of becoming lost or damaged,

chunks.en: brings them in one pair at a time.
chunks.explain: He wears them, the way we wear tefillin.
chunks.st: brings them in to his house pair by pair
chunks.stMore: by donning them in the manner in which they are typically donned for the mitzva.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: two pairs at a time.
chunks.st: He brings them in two pairs by two pairs.

chunks.en: When does this apply?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement that one is permitted to carry phylacteries inside said?

chunks.en: With old ones. But with new ones,
chunks.st: It is with regard to old phylacteries, which have already been used and are designated for the mitzva. However, with regard to new ones,
chunks.stMore: as it is unclear whether they are phylacteries or merely amulets in the form of phylacteries,

chunks.en: he does not have to. If he found them tied in bundles or piles,
chunks.st: he is exempt from performing the task. If one finds phylacteries tied in bundles or in wrapped piles,
chunks.stMore: in which case he is unable to carry them in pairs,

chunks.en: he waits with them until dark and brings them in.
chunks.st: he sits there and waits with them until dark, guarding them until the conclusion of Shabbat, and then brings them in to his house.

chunks.en: And when it is dangerous, he covers them and goes on his way.
chunks.st: And in a time of danger, when it is dangerous to tarry outside town, he covers the phylacteries and proceeds on his way.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon says people may pass the tefillin from one to another, each less than four amos, until they reach the town. The same is done with a baby born in a field. Rabbi Yehudah says even a barrel may be passed this way, but the Sages disagree.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says
chunks.stMore: that there is an alternative method of transferring the phylacteries:

chunks.en: he gives them to his friend,
chunks.st: One gives them to another
chunks.stMore: who is less than four cubits from him,

chunks.en: and his friend to his friend,
chunks.st: and the other passes them to another,

chunks.en: until they reach the outer courtyard.
chunks.st: until the phylacteries reach the outermost courtyard
chunks.stMore: of the city. Since carrying less than four cubits in a public domain is not prohibited by Torah law, in this case, the Sages permitted carrying in that manner due to the sanctity of the phylacteries.

chunks.en: And the same with his son,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to one’s son
chunks.stMore: who was born in a field and may not be carried on Shabbat, since that is akin to carrying a burden in the public domain:

chunks.en: he gives him to his friend,
chunks.st: One gives him to another,

chunks.en: and his friend to his friend,
chunks.st: and the other passes him to another,

chunks.en: even a hundred people.
chunks.st: even if it requires a hundred people.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: a person may give a barrel to his friend,
chunks.st: A person may even give a barrel to another,

chunks.en: and his friend to his friend,
chunks.st: and the other may pass it to another,

chunks.en: even past the Shabbos limit.
chunks.st: and in that way even take it beyond the Shabbat limit,
chunks.stMore: provided that no one person carries it more than four cubits.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.he: לֹא תְהַלֵּךְ זוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵרַגְלֵי בְעָלֶיהָ:
chunks.en: this barrel may not go farther than its owner's feet may go.
chunks.st: This barrel may not go a greater distance than the feet of its owner, i.e., it may not be carried any farther than its owner may walk.

mishnayos.summary: If a holy scroll rolls out of someone's hand on Shabbos into the street, the mishnah teaches when he may roll it back and when he should only turn it over so the writing faces down.

chunks.en: If he was reading a scroll on the doorstep,
chunks.st: One who was reading a sacred book in scroll form on Shabbat on an elevated, wide threshold,

chunks.en: and the scroll rolled out of his hand,
chunks.st: and the book rolled from his hand
chunks.stMore: into the public domain,

chunks.en: he rolls it back to himself.
chunks.st: he may roll it back to himself,
chunks.stMore: since one of its ends remains in his hand.

chunks.en: If he was reading on top of the roof,
chunks.st: If he was reading on top the roof,
chunks.stMore: which is a full-fledged private domain,

chunks.en: and the scroll rolled out of his hand,
chunks.st: and the book rolled from his hand,

chunks.en: as long as it did not reach ten tefachim from the ground,
chunks.st: as long as the edge of the book did not reach within ten handbreadths
chunks.stMore: above the public domain, the book is still in its own domain, and he may

chunks.en: he rolls it back to himself.
chunks.st: roll it back to himself.

chunks.en: Once it reached ten tefachim,
chunks.st: However, once the book has reached within ten handbreadths
chunks.stMore: above the public domain, it is prohibited to roll the book back to oneself.

chunks.en: he turns it over onto the writing.
chunks.explain: So the holy words are not facing up and shamed.
chunks.st: In that case, he may only turn it over onto the side with writing,
chunks.stMore: so that the writing of the book will be facedown and not exposed and degraded.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even if it is only raised from
chunks.st: Even if the scroll is removed only a needle breadth from the ground,

chunks.en: the ground by the thickness of a needle,
chunks.st: he rolls it

chunks.en: he rolls it back to himself.
chunks.st: back to himself.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even on the ground itself he rolls it back to himself,
chunks.st: Even if the scroll is on the ground itself, he rolls it back to himself,

chunks.en: because there is no rule made by the Rabbis for resting on Shabbos
chunks.st: as you have nothing that was instituted as a rabbinic decree to enhance the character of Shabbat as a day of rest

chunks.en: that stands in the way of holy writings.
chunks.st: that stands as an impediment before the rescue of sacred writings.

mishnayos.summary: We may put things on a ledge in front of a window on Shabbos. A person may stand in one area and move things in another, as long as he does not carry them more than four amos.

chunks.en: A ledge in front of a window,
chunks.st: With regard to a ledge in front of a window,
chunks.stMore: that is ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide,

chunks.en: we may put things on it and take things from it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: one may place objects upon it or remove them from it on Shabbat
chunks.stMore: via the window.

chunks.en: A person may stand in a private area
chunks.st: A person may stand in a private domain

chunks.en: and move things in the public street,
chunks.st: and move objects that are in a public domain,
chunks.stMore: as there is no concern that he might mistakenly bring them into the private domain.

chunks.en: or in the public street and move things in a private area,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may stand in a public domain and move objects in a private domain,

chunks.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא חוּץ מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת:
chunks.en: as long as he does not carry them past four amos.
chunks.st: provided that he does not carry them beyond four cubits in the public domain, which is prohibited on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not stand in one area and make water or spit into another area. Rabbi Yehudah says that once spit is gathered in his mouth, he may not walk four amos before spitting it out.

chunks.en: A person may not stand in an area
that is private and make water into the public street,
or in the public street and make water into a private area.
And he also may not spit.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
even once the spit is gathered in his mouth,

chunks.he: לֹא יְהַלֵּךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַד שֶׁיָרֹק:
chunks.en: he may not walk four amos until he spits.

mishnayos.summary: A person may not stand in one area and drink in another unless he puts his head and most of his body into the place where he drinks. The mishnah also teaches about catching rain water from a gutter or a pipe.

chunks.en: A person may not stand in an area
chunks.st: A person may stand in a private domain

chunks.en: that is private and drink in the public street,
chunks.st: and extend his head and drink in a public domain,

chunks.en: or in the public street and drink in a private area,
chunks.st: and he may stand in a public domain and drink in a private domain,

chunks.en: unless he puts his head
chunks.st: only if he brings his head

chunks.en: and most of his body into the place where he drinks.
chunks.st: and most of his body into the domain in which he drinks.

chunks.en: And the same in a winepress.
chunks.st: And the same applies in a winepress,
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: A person may catch water from a gutter
chunks.st: A person standing in a public domain on Shabbat may catch water in a vessel from a gutter
chunks.stMore: running along the side of a roof,

chunks.en: lower than ten tefachim.
chunks.st: if it is less than ten handbreadths
chunks.stMore: off the ground, which is part of the public domain.

chunks.en: And from a pipe,
chunks.st: And from a pipe
chunks.stMore: that protrudes from the roof,

chunks.en: he may drink in any way.
chunks.st: one may drink in any manner, i.e., not only by catching the water in a vessel, but even by pressing his mouth directly against the spout.

mishnayos.summary: A water pit or a garbage pile in the street that is ten tefachim high counts as a private area, so we may take water from it or pour water onto it through a window above it.

chunks.en: A pit in the public street,
chunks.st: With regard to a cistern in a public domain,

chunks.en: with a wall around it ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: with an embankment ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the embankment constitutes a private domain by itself,

chunks.he: חַלּוֹן שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו מְמַלְּאִין הֵימֶנּוּ בְשַׁבָּת.
chunks.en: from a window above it we may take water from it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: if there is a window above the cistern, i.e., the window of an adjacent house is situated above the cistern, one may draw water from the cistern on Shabbat
chunks.stMore: through the window, as it is permitted to carry from one private domain to another.

chunks.he: אַשְׁפָּה בִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: A garbage pile in the public street ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to a garbage dump in a public domain that is ten handbreadths high,
chunks.stMore: which means it has the status of a private domain,

chunks.en: from a window above it we may pour
chunks.st: if there is a window above the pile of refuse that abuts the garbage dump, one may throw water

chunks.en: water onto it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: from the window onto the dump on Shabbat, as it is permitted to carry from one private domain to another.

mishnayos.summary: Under a tree whose branches come down close to the ground, we may carry, but we may not sit on its high roots. Some doors and mats may only be used to close an opening on Shabbos if they hang above the ground.

chunks.en: A tree that hangs down over the ground,
chunks.st: With regard to a tree that was hanging over the ground,
chunks.stMore: i.e., its branches hung down on all sides like a tent so that it threw a shadow on the ground,

chunks.en: if its branches are not higher
chunks.st: if the tips of its branches are no higher

chunks.en: than three tefachim from the ground,
chunks.st: than three handbreadths from the ground, one

chunks.en: we may carry under it.
chunks.st: may carry under it.
chunks.stMore: This applies even if the tree is planted in a public domain, as the branches form partitions which turn the enclosed area into a private domain.

chunks.he: שָׁרָשָׁיו גְּבוֹהִין מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: If its roots are three tefachim above the ground,
chunks.st: If its roots were three handbreadths higher than the ground, one

chunks.en: he may not sit on them.
chunks.st: may not sit on them,
chunks.stMore: as it is prohibited to use a tree on Shabbat. Any part of a tree that is three handbreadths above the ground has the status of a tree with regard to this prohibition.

chunks.en: A back-yard door, thorns that fill a gap, and mats,
chunks.st: With regard to the door to a rear court, i.e., a door that opens from a house to the courtyard situated behind it, which is typically not a proper door but merely a wooden board without hinges that closes off the doorway; and likewise bundles of thorns that seal a breach; and reed mats, one

chunks.en: we may not close with them,
chunks.st: may not close an opening with them
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat. This would be considered building or completing a building,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גְּבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ:
chunks.en: unless they are held up off the ground.
chunks.st: unless they remain above the ground even when they are open.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir says a person may not stand in one area and unlock a door in another unless he is inside a wall. The Sages tell of a market in Yerushalayim where the key was kept in a window above the door.

chunks.en: A person may not stand in an area
chunks.st: A person may not stand in the private domain

chunks.en: that is private and open a door in the public street,
chunks.st: and open a door located in the public domain
chunks.stMore: with a key, lest he inadvertently transfer the key from one domain to the other.

chunks.en: or in the public street and open one in a private area,
chunks.st: Likewise, one may not stand in the public domain and open a door in the private domain

chunks.en: unless he made
chunks.st: with a key, unless

chunks.en: a wall ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: in the latter case he erected a partition ten handbreadths high
chunks.stMore: around the door and stands inside it.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְשׁוּק שֶׁל פַּטָּמִין שֶׁהָיָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
chunks.en: There was a story in the market of the poultry sellers in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: There was an incident at the poultry dealers’ market in Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: where they would fatten fowl for slaughter (Rabbeinu Ḥananel),

chunks.en: where they would lock up and put the key
chunks.st: and they would lock the doors to their shops and place the key

chunks.en: in the window above the door.
chunks.st: in the window that was over the door,

mishnayos.summary: Some door bolts may be used to lock a door in the Beis HaMikdash on Shabbos but not elsewhere, because the Rabbis' Shabbos rules were not made for the Beis HaMikdash. Rabbi Yehudah disagrees about which bolts.

chunks.st: With regard to a bolt that is attached to the door, but owing to the length of the rope, it does not hang from the door but drags along the ground,

chunks.en: we may lock with it in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: one may lock a door with it in the Temple
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat, as this is prohibited only by rabbinic decree, issued to enhance the character of Shabbat as a day of rest, and rabbinic decrees are not in effect in the Temple.

chunks.en: but not out in the country.

chunks.st: And with regard to one that is not tied at all but rests entirely on the ground, it is prohibited in both

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

mishnayos.summary: In the Beis HaMikdash we may put a door's lower pin back in place on Shabbos, but not elsewhere. The upper pin is forbidden everywhere. Rabbi Yehudah disagrees.

mishnayos.summary: In the Beis HaMikdash on Shabbos we may put back a bandage, tie a harp string, and cut off a wart by hand, but not elsewhere. Doing it for the first time, or with a tool, is forbidden everywhere.

chunks.en: We may put back a bandage in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: One may return to its place a bandage that became detached from a wound on Shabbat in the Temple.
chunks.stMore: In the Temple, this is not prohibited as a preventive measure, lest one come to spread the ointment and thereby perform the prohibited labor of smoothing.

chunks.en: but not out in the country.
chunks.st: However, one may not return a bandage to its place in the rest of the country.

mishnayos.summary: If a dead sheretz is found in the Beis HaMikdash on Shabbos, a Kohen takes it out. The Rabbis argue how to carry it, and from which parts it must be taken out. Rabbi Shimon says the Sages only allowed things forbidden by the Rabbis.
